title: Why America Had THREE EV Plugs (and Who Won) 🔌⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: Why did America end up with three different fast-charging plugs for electric cars? A format war.
Round one, twenty ten: Japan's CHAdeMO, backed by Tokyo Electric Power and Nissan. The Leaf used it.
Round two: CCS. The regular AC plug, with two extra DC pins added underneath.
Meanwhile, Tesla made its own plug in twenty twelve. Smaller, and the same two pins carry AC and DC.
In late twenty twenty-two, Tesla opened the design as NACS. Ford signed on, then GM, then nearly everyone.
By twenty twenty-four it was official: SAE J thirty-four hundred.
Should one company's plug become everyone's standard? Follow EV Drive.
